# Built-in Functions

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_builtins_doc.py -->

JarLang has 127 built-in functions. Functions marked with (native) also work with the native compiler.

Functions that take a list take it as the first argument, so `xs.map(f)` and `xs |> map(f)` are the same as `map(xs, f)`.

### Constants

* `pi` (or `π`): π ≈ 3.14159, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter
* `tau` (or `τ`): τ = 2π ≈ 6.28318
* `e`: Euler's number ≈ 2.71828
* `phi` (or `φ`): the golden ratio φ ≈ 1.61803
* `inf` (or `∞`): positive infinity
* `nan`: not-a-number

### Input and Output

* `exit(code=0)` (native): Stop the program with an exit code.
* `input(prompt="")` (native): Read a line of text from the user.
* `plot(f, a=nil, b=nil, width=60, height=15)`: Plot a function over [a, b] (default [-10, 10]) or a list of numbers, in the terminal.
* `print(...values)` (native): Print values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
* `read_file(path)`: Return the contents of a text file.
* `write(...values)` (native): Print values separated by spaces, without a trailing newline.
* `write_file(path, text)`: Write text to a file (replacing it).

### Math

* `abs(x)` (native): Absolute value.
* `acos(x)` (native): Inverse cosine, in radians.
* `asin(x)` (native): Inverse sine, in radians.
* `atan(x)` (native): Inverse tangent, in radians.
* `atan2(y, x)` (native): Angle of the point (x, y) from the positive x-axis, in radians.
* `cbrt(x)` (native): Cube root.
* `ceil(x)` (native): Round up to an integer.
* `choose(n, k)`: Binomial coefficient: ways to choose k items from n.
* `clamp(x, lo, hi)` (native): Limit x to the range [lo, hi].
* `cos(x)` (native): Cosine (radians).
* `cosh(x)` (native): Hyperbolic cosine.
* `deg(x)` (native): Convert radians to degrees.
* `divisors(n)`: All positive divisors of n, in increasing order.
* `exp(x)` (native): e raised to the power x.
* `factorial(n)` (native): Factorial of n, also written n! (floats use the gamma function).
* `factors(n)`: Prime factorization, e.g. factors(360) == [2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 5].
* `floor(x)` (native): Round down to an integer.
* `gcd(a, b)` (native): Greatest common divisor.
* `hypot(x, y)` (native): Length of the hypotenuse √(x² + y²).
* `is_prime(n)` (native): True if n is a prime number.
* `isqrt(n)` (native): Integer square root, the largest k where k^2 <= n.
* `lcm(a, b)` (native): Least common multiple.
* `linspace(start, stop, count)`: `count` evenly spaced floats from start to stop (inclusive).
* `ln(x)` (native): Natural logarithm.
* `log(x, base=nil)` (native): Natural logarithm, or logarithm in `base` when given.
* `log10(x)` (native): Base-10 logarithm.
* `log2(x)` (native): Base-2 logarithm.
* `max(...values)` (native): Largest of the arguments (or of a single list).
* `min(...values)` (native): Smallest of the arguments (or of a single list).
* `perm(n, k)`: Number of ordered arrangements of k items from n.
* `pow(base, exponent)` (native): base raised to exponent (same as base ^ exponent).
* `primes(limit)`: All primes up to and including `limit` (sieve of Eratosthenes).
* `rad(x)` (native): Convert degrees to radians.
* `round(x, digits=nil)` (native): Round to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), or to `digits` decimals.
* `sign(x)` (native): -1, 0 or 1 depending on the sign of x.
* `sin(x)` (native): Sine (radians).
* `sinh(x)` (native): Hyperbolic sine.
* `sqrt(x)` (native): Square root (also written √x).
* `tan(x)` (native): Tangent (radians).
* `tanh(x)` (native): Hyperbolic tangent.
* `trunc(x)` (native): Round toward zero to an integer.

### Statistics

* `mean(xs)`: Arithmetic mean (average).
* `median(xs)`: Middle value.
* `mode(xs)`: Most common value.
* `product(...values)` (native): Product of a list (or of the arguments).
* `stdev(xs)`: Sample standard deviation.
* `sum(...values)` (native): Sum of a list (or of the arguments).
* `variance(xs)`: Sample variance.

### Lists

* `chunk(xs, size)`: Split into lists of `size` items.
* `contains(coll, item)` (native): True if the collection contains the item (same as `item in coll`).
* `copy(x)`: A shallow copy of a list or dict.
* `count(coll, item)`: How many items equal `item` (or satisfy it, if it is a function).
* `drop(xs, n)`: Everything except the first n items.
* `enumerate(xs, start=0)`: List of [index, item] pairs, for use with `for i, x in enumerate(xs)`.
* `first(xs)`: The first item (nil if empty).
* `flatten(xs)`: Flatten one level of nesting, e.g. flatten([[1, 2], [3]]) == [1, 2, 3].
* `index_of(coll, item)` (native): Position of the first occurrence of item, or -1.
* `insert(xs, index, value)`: Insert a value before `index` (in place) and return the list.
* `join(xs, sep="")` (native): Join items into a string: join([1, 2, 3], ", ") == "1, 2, 3".
* `last(xs)`: The last item (nil if empty).
* `len(x)` (native): Number of items in a list, string, dict or range.
* `pop(xs, index=-1)` (native): Remove and return the last item (or the item at `index`).
* `push(xs, ...values)` (native): Append values to a list (in place) and return the list.
* `range(a, b=nil, step=1)` (native): range(stop), range(start, stop) or range(start, stop, step), not including stop.
* `remove(coll, item)`: Remove the first occurrence of `item` from a list, or a key from a dict.
* `reverse(xs)` (native): A reversed copy of a list or string.
* `sort(xs, key=nil)` (native): A sorted copy of a list, optionally ordered by `key(item)`.
* `take(xs, n)`: The first n items.
* `unique(xs)`: Items with duplicates removed (first occurrence wins).
* `zip(...seqs)`: Pair up items: zip([1, 2], ["a", "b"]) == [[1, "a"], [2, "b"]].

### Functions

* `all(xs, f=nil)`: True if every item is truthy (or satisfies `f`).
* `any(xs, f=nil)`: True if any item is truthy (or satisfies `f`).
* `compose(f, g)`: compose(f, g)(x) == f(g(x)).
* `each(xs, f)`: Call `f` on every item (for side effects).
* `filter(xs, f)`: Keep the items for which `f(item)` is truthy.
* `find(xs, f)`: The first item for which `f(item)` is truthy, or nil.
* `map(xs, f)`: Apply `f` to every item: map([1, 2, 3], fn(x) => x * 2) == [2, 4, 6].
* `memoize(f)`: A version of `f` that remembers its results, like `fib = memoize(fib)`.
* `reduce(xs, f, initial=nil)`: Combine items left to right: reduce([1, 2, 3], fn(a, b) => a + b) == 6.

### Strings

* `chars(s)` (native): List of the characters in a string.
* `chr(code)` (native): One-character string for a Unicode code point.
* `ends_with(s, suffix)` (native): True if s ends with suffix.
* `is_alpha(s)`: True if the string is non-empty and all letters.
* `is_digit(s)`: True if the string is non-empty and all digits.
* `lines(s)`: List of the lines in a string.
* `lower(s)` (native): Lowercase copy of a string.
* `ord(ch)` (native): Unicode code point of a one-character string.
* `pad(s, width, fill=" ")`: Pad on the left to `width` (negative width pads on the right).
* `replace(s, old, new)` (native): Replace every occurrence of `old` with `new`.
* `split(s, sep=nil)` (native): Split a string on `sep` (default: any whitespace).
* `starts_with(s, prefix)` (native): True if s starts with prefix.
* `trim(s)` (native): Copy without leading/trailing whitespace.
* `upper(s)` (native): Uppercase copy of a string.

### Dicts

* `get(d, key, default=nil)`: d[key] if present, otherwise `default` (nil).
* `has(d, key)`: True if the dict has the key.
* `items(d)`: List of [key, value] pairs, for use with `for k, v in items(d)`.
* `keys(d)`: List of a dict's keys.
* `values(d)`: List of a dict's values.

### Conversions

* `bin(n)`: Binary text for an integer, e.g. bin(5) == "0b101".
* `bool(value)`: Convert to true or false (nil, false, 0, "", [] and {} are false).
* `dict(pairs=nil)`: Make a dict from a list of [key, value] pairs.
* `float(value)` (native): Convert to a floating-point number.
* `fmt(value, spec)`: Format a value with a format spec, e.g. fmt(pi, ".3f") == "3.142".
* `hex(n)`: Hexadecimal text for an integer, e.g. hex(255) == "0xff".
* `int(value, base=10)` (native): Convert to an integer (floats are truncated, strings can use a `base`).
* `list(value=nil)`: Make a list from a range, string, dict (its keys) or list.
* `repr(value)`: Text form of a value with strings quoted.
* `str(value)` (native): Convert any value to its text form.
* `type(value)`: The name of a value's type, e.g. "int" or "list".

### Random Numbers

* `choice(xs)`: A random element of a list.
* `randint(lo, hi)`: A random integer in [lo, hi] (inclusive).
* `random()`: A random float in [0, 1).
* `seed(n)`: Seed the random number generator for reproducible results.
* `shuffle(xs)`: A shuffled copy of a list.

### Other

* `assert(cond, message="assertion failed")` (native): Stop with an error if `cond` is false.
* `clock()` (native): Seconds elapsed on a high-resolution timer (for measuring code).
* `doc(value)`: The documentation text of a function.
* `error(message)`: Raise an error (catchable with try/catch).
* `help(value=nil)`: Show documentation for a function (or list all builtins).
* `sleep(seconds)`: Pause for a number of seconds.
